Every outbound network call must have an explicit timeout/cancellation path and must not silently reuse stale connection state. Concretely: (1) Apply an AbortSignal/timeout to every fetch or socket call on a given operation, including fallback paths — a primary request can be bounded while its fallback (e.g. a bare `fetch` with no timeout) hangs indefinitely against a host that drops packets instead of refusing, which can block an entire feature (e.g. task start) rather than just a secondary UI surface. (2) When introducing custom transports, dispatchers, or proxy agents, preserve existing routing semantics for special addresses such as loopback/local-network hosts — libraries like undici's `EnvHttpProxyAgent` will proxy `127.0.0.1` whenever `HTTP_PROXY` is set and `NO_PROXY` isn't, which silently breaks local model servers; detect local/loopback targets and route them through a direct, no-proxy agent while everything else goes through the proxy-aware path, and add regression tests with the proxy env vars set and `NO_PROXY` unset. (3) When connection-identifying parameters change (host, credentials, control path, etc.), explicitly close/invalidate the old connection or socket and remove it from any cache before creating a new one, so later operations can't reuse a connection tied to stale credentials. Document any known gaps (e.g. DNS names resolving to local addresses) and the reasoning for not resolving them at configuration time if resolving would add unacceptable latency or dependency on transient state.
